answer: Adaptive Arrival-Spacing Gate. Each identity must build a slow spiral of heartbeat timing: intervals lengthen by a fixed ratio over its first hundred packets, and the gate admits traffic only when observed spacing tracks the declared curve within tolerance. Clones launched in parallel diverge from a human-paced thread of activity and get throttled to one packet per long window. The attacker pays real elapsed time per identity, plus a calibration lantern cost to re-tune each clone against the curve.
